sara-ops: Hey payroll — my May paystub looks wrong. I moved to Toronto (permanent) on 2025-05-12 but my pay shows US FICA + Canadian CPP both deducted for the same earnings. Net is way lower. Anyone see this? :grimacing:
canada-payroll: Hi @sara-ops, sorry to hear that. Can you paste the paystub lines or DM a screenshot (mask acct)?
sara-ops: Pasting redacted lines: 
```
Period: 2025-05-01 to 2025-05-15
Gross: 3,200.00 USD
Federal tax (US): -420.00 USD
State tax (WA): -0.00 USD
FICA (Social Security): -198.40 USD
CPP (Canada): -160.00 CAD
EI (Canada): -45.00 CAD
Health premium: -32.00 USD
Net paid: 1,xxx.xx (converted to CAD in bank)
```
canada-payroll: Thanks. Looks like the payroll feeds included both a US resident payroll row and a Canadian resident row in the same run. The system didn't clear the US payroll residency flags before the Canada conversion.
emma-hr: To confirm: employee relocation was logged in People Ops on 2025-05-09 and the new work location set to Canada in Workday on 2025-05-10. We also submitted the CRA registration and T4 enrolment requests.
us-payroll: Our US payroll export for mid-May still had you on the US tax residency table because a termination date wasn't applied before the run. So US taxes were processed. Meanwhile Canadian export was created for the new hire record and CPP/EI were applied. That's why both sets of deductions appear.
payroll-bot: Ticket created: PR-9921 "Mid-month relocation: dual FICA/CPP deductions for sara-ops May 2025". Assigned to GlobalPay ops. Initial ETA 72 hours.
sara-ops: Ouch. Will this require tax filings in both countries? Concerned about extra withholding and year-end forms (W-2/T4).
tax-advisor: Short answer: likely not permanent double taxation, but documentation and filings will be needed. We'll need to: 1) correct payroll records (reverse duplicate FICA if US reporting occurs for wages after Canadian residency), 2) request refund/reclaim where applicable, 3) prepare explanatory attachments for both CRA and IRS if both reports were generated. Please keep receipts and corrected paystubs.\an:emma-hr: @tax-advisor can you outline the steps for reclaim timeline? Also need to know whether we should process a one-time net top-up to cover the shortfall while reclaim is in progress.
tax-advisor: Reclaim timelines: US FICA refund requests can take 6-12 weeks with US provider processing; CRA CPP/EI adjustments usually processed within 4-8 weeks but vary. For employee cashflow we commonly do a one-time net make-whole payment and then reconcile once refunds are received. That avoids hardship for the employee.
canada-payroll: Operational next steps we will take: 1) Suspend any further Canadian deductions pending coordination (so future runs don't double up), 2) Add an adjustment on the June run to reverse the duplicate US FICA if provider allows, 3) Post a separate correction showing the net top-up as a non-taxable reimbursement if we net-gross it appropriately, 4) Generate corrected payroll XMLs for provider submission to CRA/IRS.
us-payroll: We'll also audit other recent movers to ensure the residency-termination flag is reliably set before US runs. Looks like a workflow gap between HR location change and payroll termination step.
emma-hr: I'll add a temporary checklist item: when rescinding US residency we must create a termination event in Payroll system with effective date = last US day, and confirm the new local hire export queued before the next payroll close.
sara-ops: I appreciate the plan. Please confirm whether I can get the net top-up on the June 1 payroll if the refund isn't back by then.
payroll-bot: PR-9921 updated: requested net-top-up approval. Finance and Payroll leads to approve by 2025-05-20.
canada-payroll: Confirmed tentatively: we can issue a one-time net top-up on June payroll and mark it as "relocation shortfall reimbursement". Final approval pending finance. We will also attach corrected paystubs and a note for year-end reporting.
sara-ops: Thanks team. Can you also confirm currency conversion handling? My bank got funds in CAD at a poor FX rate and I lost ~40 CAD on the conversion.\an:tax-advisor: For future mid-month moves we recommend running the payroll in the destination currency when possible and instructing bank to expect incoming currency to minimize conversions. We'll add this as an ops note.
emma-hr: Noted. I'll update the relocation SOP and include an explicit pre-payroll cutover step to lock currency/residency flags.
sara-ops: Great, thanks all. Ping me if you need any more docs from my side. :pray:
